# Security control matrix

Every material threat needs an owner, enforcement point, verification method, and residual-risk decision.

| Boundary | Minimum evidence | Verification |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Identity | actor inventory, authentication strength, lifecycle owner | invalid, expired, revoked, recovery cases |
| Authorization | policy subject/resource/action, deny default | cross-tenant and privilege-escalation tests |
| Data | classification, residency, retention, encryption/key owner | access audit, restore, deletion proof |
| Network | trust boundaries, ingress/egress policy, service identity | segmentation and egress-deny tests |
| Supply chain | locked dependencies, provenance, artifact integrity | vulnerability and signature gates |
| Secrets | storage, rotation, break-glass, redaction | leak scan and revoked-secret test |
| Abuse | quotas, rate limits, fraud/automation signals | bypass, exhaustion, distributed abuse |
| Operations | least privilege, approvals, audit, incident owner | emergency access and evidence review |

Compliance names are constraints, not proof. Map each applicable control to concrete implementation and current evidence.
